by_judge.judge: S.G.PANDIT & R DEVDAS & K. V. ARAVIND

narrative:
On October 8, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 46.1%, with 1,393 of the 3,021 scheduled matters taken up across 55 judges. This represents an efficiency gain compared to preceding sessions, where hearing rates stood at 40.8% on October 7, 39.6% on October 6, and 41.7% on October 5.

Bench efficiency varied considerably across court halls. Among benches handling substantial daily dockets, Justice K.S. Hemalekha led with a 90.3% clearance rate (28 of 31 heard), followed by Justice T.P. Vivekananda at 83.3% (45 of 54 heard) and Justice S. Vishwajith Shetty at 78.1% (75 of 96 heard in Hall 21). Conversely, the Chief Justice bench heard none of its 32 scheduled matters, while Justice B.M. Shyam Prasad took up only 14.8% of his primary cause list (25 of 169 heard), and Justice Geetha K.B. processed 19.0% (20 of 105 heard).

At the procedural stage level, interlocutory and preliminary stages showed improved throughput. Orders, the largest stage category, achieved a 48.1% hearing rate (499 of 1,038 heard), up from 41.7% on October 7. Preliminary hearings converted at 53.5% (307 of 574), and regular admissions reached 46.6% (311 of 667). Final hearings lagged at 29.8% (165 of 553 heard), dipping slightly from 31.5% the prior day, though remaining higher than October 6's 19.3%.

Writ Petitions (WP) formed the largest caseload with 1,186 listings, recording a notable clearance rate of 52.4% (622 heard), up from 41.0% on October 7. In contrast, Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) struggled at 31.0% (167 of 538 heard), while Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) maintained stable clearance at 44.5% (185 of 416 heard). Specialized matters showed mixed progress: Criminal Revision Petitions saw high conversion at 72.5%, whereas Writ Appeals cleared at just 25.5%.
